title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Context (pp. 95-99): Grothendieck is building a combinatorial 'analysis situs' (a tame-topology-style foundation). The data are a set M with a symmetric relation '||' (read 'orthogonal' or 'separated'). For X ⊂ M, Cosupp(X) is the set of points orthogonal to every point of X, written ∁X. Supp(X) = Cosupp(Cosupp X) is the double orthogonal, a Galois-type closure. The 'supports' (closed sets) form a complete lattice Σ with join S∨S' = Supp(S∪S') and orthocomplement ∁. On p.97 he is proving that a map φ from subsets of an index set I to Σ is a lattice embedding commuting with Sup/Inf. To do this he must show S_{A∖B} = S_A ∩ ∁S_B, which he reduces to Lemma 3: if S || S' then S' = (S∨S') ∩ ∁S. In lattice language this is exactly the orthomodular law of an ortholattice: a ⊥ b ⇒ b = (a∨b) ∧ a^⊥. On p.98 he refutes it with a graph whose orthogonality is adjacency, the path A'–A–B–B'. Cosupp{A} = {A',B} and Supp{A} = Cosupp{A',B} = {A}, so {A} is closed. Likewise Cosupp{B} = {A,B'} and {B} is closed. A || B since they are adjacent. Cosupp(A∪B) = ∁A∩∁B = ∅ because no vertex is adjacent to both, so A∨B = M. Lemma 3 would then force A = ∁B and B = ∁A, i.e. {A} = {A,B'}, which is false ('Ridicule...'). In fact the closed sets here are ∅, {A}, {B}, {A',B}, {A,B'} and M, i.e. the hexagon ortholattice O6. This is the textbook minimal non-orthomodular ortholattice. He concludes that the general hypothetical theory needs an extra axiom ensuring S_{A−B} = S_A∩∁S_B, which he finds 'a bit brutal'. Still, he suspects it holds for genuine varieties under the divisibility hypothesis (AtL1), the same one he used to give an intrinsic meaning to 'constructible supports'. On p.99 he indeed decides to admit AtL1 in addition to AtL2 and AtL3.
errors: Lemma 3 (p.97) is false in the stated generality; Grothendieck himself detects this (marginal 'Faux', then the counterexample here). It amounts to assuming orthomodularity of the lattice of supports, which fails for general orthogonality spaces.
The page writes 'supp A = cosupp{A',B} = A''; for the argument to work (and by direct computation) it must be '= A' (the set {A}). Likely a slip of the pen or a misreading.

ideas.what: Lattice of 'supports' as Galois-closed sets of a symmetric orthogonality relation, with ∁ as orthocomplement
ideas.modern_name: Complete ortholattice of an orthogonality space (biorthogonal closure)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished Analysis situs notes (cote 156-7)

ideas.what: Lemma 3: S || S' ⇒ S' = (S∨S')∩∁S, needed for S_{A−B} = S_A∩∁S_B
ideas.usually_credited_to: Husimi (1937), Birkhoff–von Neumann quantum logic tradition

ideas.what: Counterexample: path graph on 4 vertices with adjacency as orthogonality gives a non-orthomodular lattice of closed sets
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon O6 as the lattice of a Dacey graph (P4); non-orthomodularity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the orthomodular-lattice / Dacey-graph literature (Dacey 1968; Sumner)

ideas.what: Conjecture that the formula holds for actual 'varieties' under a divisibility axiom (AtL1), tied to constructible supports
ideas.modern_name: Boolean or orthomodular behaviour of support lattices in tame (o-minimal-like) geometry; cf. regular open sets forming a Boolean algebra

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics for supports in his combinatorial analysis situs runs into exactly the orthomodularity question of quantum logic. He rediscovers the hexagon O6 as an obstruction via a graph. The link between tame-topology foundations and orthogonality spaces / orthomodular lattices is not made explicit in his circulated writings, though it is mathematically elementary.
missed.quote: Le lemme affirme donc que A = ∁B, B = ∁A, ce qui est faux! Ridicule...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It indicates that the axiom he later adds (AtL1, divisibility) plays the role of an orthomodularity or Boolean axiom for support lattices. That could be of interest for reconstructing his 1986 'tame topology' program, but is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a self-correction: a false lemma (orthomodular law) refuted by a small graph counterexample yielding the well-known O6 lattice. It is historically interesting as a glimpse of how his Analysis situs axioms evolved toward AtL1, but contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'supp A = cosupp {A', B} = A'' should almost certainly read '= A' (the singleton {A}), as the mathematics requires.
'par ce que [?] sont liés: A et B à finis [?]!' is roughly a marginal remark that no vertex is linked to both A and B; the exact wording is uncertain.

'des th. [?] hypothétiques dégagées d'hypothèses déroutantes' is uncertain; the sense is 'the collection of hypothetical theories ... would require axioms such that the relevant formula S_{A−B} = S_A∩∁S_B holds'.
